text:
Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes

The triage app gives you the order to do things in, and this section is about doing them in a way that takes pressure off the person.

Anything that could let someone hurt themselves in the next five minutes takes priority, so get the car keys out of reach and turn the stove off, and move them away from roads and balconies, or pools of water for that matter. Letting them move around is fine, and pacing can help, but keep them from taking more of any substance. If they want to go confront somebody, that can wait. And if they want to leave, have someone go with them. Put any weapons away and keep the person away from crowds and strangers. If they want to post their big revelation about the universe, or message an ex, take the phone.

A lot of what looks like a deep psychedelic crisis is a scared person in a room that's getting on their nerves, so look around the room next. They're feeling overwhelmed, so dim the lights, and clear out the extra people around them. Move them away from anyone they're wary of as well, and check whether they're just too hot or too cold, or desperate for the bathroom.

placement: the first half of the Psychological First Aid section of the Shadow Work part: the dangers and the room, before the script that reminds them where they are

opens.first_sentence: Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes
opens.why_reading: the heading tells someone looking after a person in a bad state that this is what to do now, in the first five minutes, which is their case; the next line says the triage app sets the order and this section is how to do it without adding pressure

same_point: the room's two paragraphs made one point, what in the room to fix: merged here, the fixes paragraph (B240) is deleted and its sentence follows the reason; none else: read the section from its heading to Stillness or Movement? for the dangers, the room, the reminder of where they are, the practice script and care, and the pointer to the next sections (the last paragraph's 'one calm person' is the Get One Human Anchor pointer, not the room's extra people)

questions.Q1: PASS: each paragraph opens on its point: the section's job, the first priority, then why to look at the room
questions.Q2: PASS: every act is the helper's own, with its purpose: the dangers removed, the lights dimmed and the extra people out because they're overwhelmed, the person moved away from anyone they're wary of, their body checked
questions.Q3: PASS: which things exactly: keys, stove, roads, balconies, pools, weapons, the phone; the lights, the extra people, anyone they're wary of, heat, cold, the bathroom
questions.Q4: PASS: no terms a reader wouldn't know; the triage app is linked where it is named
questions.Q5: PASS: each so turns on what's said before it: the room is often the cause, so look at it; they're overwhelmed, so dim and clear
questions.Q6: PASS: dangers, then the room: its reason, its two fixes, then the people near them and the person's own body
questions.Q7: PASS: every fact is about the person in front of them now
questions.Q8: PASS: the room's fixes sit together after its reason; the person's body is checked with the room, as before
questions.Q9: PASS: nothing compressed: an act or a pair of acts a sentence, with the small words that carry the reason ('so', 'as well', 'just')

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
